story.soThat: services can get an authenticated client instance
story.tasks:
- T1 – Implement client wrapper - Create `src/lib/keycloak/client.ts` that: - Imports `loadConfig()` from `src/lib/keycloak/config.ts`. - Constructs a `KcAdminClient` with `baseUrl` and `realmName` derived from config. - Performs password-grant authentication using config credentials. - Export a `getKeycloakClient()` function that returns a cached instance (singleton) and performs lazy authentication on first use.
- T2 – Handle auth errors cleanly - Ensure authentication errors are thrown in a way that later stories (error/logging) can wrap into `IdentiKeyError` without double-logging or losing stack traces. - Avoid logging secrets or full URLs with embedded credentials.
- T3 – Unit tests / integration shim - Add tests (or a test harness) that: - Verify `getKeycloakClient()` calls `loadConfig()` and constructs the admin client with correct base URL and realm. - Verify singleton behavior (same instance returned on multiple calls). - Are structured so they can be wired to a real Keycloak instance later, but do not require one in this repo yet (e.g. by mocking `@keycloak/keycloak-admin-client`).
- T4 – Prepare for connection validation - Sketch (but do not fully implement) a `validateConnection()` helper or hook location aligned with `tech-spec-epic-1.md` so that Story 1.5 can plug in the actual validation logic without refactoring the wrapper.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Authenticated client from env configuration - Given valid Keycloak credentials are available in environment variables (loaded via `loadConfig()` from Story 1.2) When I call `getKeycloakClient()` Then I receive an authenticated `KcAdminClient` instance configured for the correct `KEYCLOAK_URL` and `KEYCLOAK_REALM`.
2. Password grant support (FR2) - And the client is authenticated using password grant with `KEYCLOAK_USERNAME`, `KEYCLOAK_PASSWORD`, and `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID` (`admin-cli` by default).
3. Service account extensibility (FR1) - And the wrapper is structured so that service-account based authentication can be added later without breaking callers (e.g. by allowing an alternate auth strategy or config extension).
4. Singleton client instance - And the client is cached as a singleton per process so that repeated calls to `getKeycloakClient()` reuse the same underlying `KcAdminClient` instance.
5. Token refresh behavior - And re-authentication or token refresh happens automatically (leveraging the underlying client’s behavior) so that services can make multiple calls without manually reauthenticating.

doc.title: keycloak-commander — Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: The system must authenticate to the Keycloak Admin API using configured credentials, support password-grant authentication initially, and be structured so that service-account based authentication can be added without breaking existing flows.

doc.title: keycloak-commander — Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: As a developer, I want a wrapper around @keycloak/keycloak-admin-client so that services can get an authenticated client instance, using configuration loaded from environment variables and supporting future authentication strategies.

doc.title: Architecture — keycloak-commander
doc.snippet: The architecture defines `src/lib/keycloak/client.ts` as the single entrypoint for obtaining an authenticated `KcAdminClient`, built on top of the configuration layer from `config.ts` and reused by all domain services.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Epic 1 – Foundation
doc.snippet: The Epic 1 tech spec defines a Keycloak client wrapper that exposes a `getKeycloakClient()` API, uses password-grant authentication based on the validated configuration, and reserves a clear extension point for future connection validation and service-account support.

artifact.reason: Provides the singleton, authenticated `KcAdminClient` instance used by all Keycloak-related services.
Verifies configuration usage, singleton semantics, and error behavior of the client wrapper.
Declares `@keycloak/keycloak-admin-client`, testing libraries, and supporting runtime dependencies used by the client wrapper.

story-context.constraints: - All services must obtain a Keycloak admin client via `getKeycloakClient()`; they should not construct `KcAdminClient` instances directly. - The wrapper must not log or otherwise expose secrets or tokens; errors should be structured for later wrapping into domain-specific error types. - The client wrapper should remain agnostic to specific interfaces (CLI, MCP, future Web UI) and focus purely on authentication and lifecycle. - The design must leave room to introduce service-account authentication and explicit connection validation (Story 1.5) without breaking callers.
story-context.interfaces: - Keycloak Client Wrapper API: - `async getKeycloakClient(): Promise<KcAdminClient>` - Behavior: - Lazily creates and authenticates a `KcAdminClient` using configuration from `loadConfig()`. - Caches the client instance for reuse on subsequent calls within the same process. - Surfaces authentication errors in a way that higher layers can wrap into project-specific error types.

tests.standards: Use Vitest for unit tests in a Node environment, mocking `@keycloak/keycloak-admin-client` and focusing on configuration usage, authentication calls, and singleton semantics. Avoid real network calls or dependence on a live Keycloak instance.
tests.ideas: - AC1: With valid configuration, `getKeycloakClient()` constructs a `KcAdminClient` with correct base URL and realm and performs password-grant authentication once. - AC2: Multiple calls to `getKeycloakClient()` return the same underlying client instance without re-instantiating. - AC3: When authentication fails, the wrapper propagates a clear error without leaking secrets and without double-logging. - AC4: The module structure makes it straightforward to plug in a `validateConnection()` helper in a later story without changing the basic `getKeycloakClient()` contract.
